question: Does positive condition information for eventual migration activation reverse or disappear for early onset when the same eels and the same frozen held-out models are scored?
source: analysis/31 fixed original expert-corrected FIII/FIV/FV cohort (575), project-held-out logistic coefficients trained for eventual activation as in analysis/36
common_cohort: Eels eligible for fixed 90-day observation window: initiation onset recorded on/before day90, or their last receiver arrival observed at/after day90. Exclude unreconstructable source-onset dates as in analysis/42. Keep this identical cohort for every outcome.
fixed_prediction: Train two nested eventual-activation models on 5 projects (stage, length, release date +/- condition), predict held-out project; do not refit either model to early/late outcomes.
primary_endpoints: onset by day 30 among identical 90-day eligible eels
eventual source-algorithm initiation among those same eels
metrics: within-heldout-project-year pair-weighted concordance AUC (base and condition-augmented)
difference in condition AUC increment between eventual and day30 endpoints
paired independent-project bootstrap of six project-level increments (10k fixed-training reps)
competing_risk_set_decomposition: Within 90day eligible cohort classify early onset <=30 days, late onset >30 days and eventual source-onset documented, and no eventual onset; score early vs never, late vs never, and early vs late without retraining. Only compare fish within the same project-year.
inference_rule: A temporal horizon dependence of the frozen condition-information gain is described if eventual-vs-30day paired delta is positive and its 6-project resampling interval excludes zero; report exact sign-flip p and project support; even then association is not causal energetic delay.
boundaries: Eligibility at day90 depends on future receiver detections and can induce informative selection; this is NOT unbiased incident hazard estimation.
Later detections are not continuous tracking evidence and observed eventual initiation is itself an algorithmic telemetry endpoint.
The same 90day cohort holds fish fixed but distinct outcome labels necessarily induce different positive/negative pair sets; contrasts are not the same outcome comparison.
Events after day90 are still eventual initiators in the eventual endpoint; project receiver followup lengths differ.
Only six independent project contexts; many paired ranks share fish and source fold models.
Positive score difference for late vs never does not establish energy storage, seasonal mismatch, hydraulic cue selection or escapement fitness.
